text:
Mike H: Heads up — hit a prefetched-residency race on canary. Prefetch flow writes residency then fires callback; if eviction runs concurrently the callback can reintroduce a token after eviction. Anyone seen this pattern?

Anjali: can you paste a short trace/snippet?

Mike H: simplified: prefetch -> lease_mgr.claim(prefix) -> write_residency(token=T1) -> async prefetch -> on_prefetch_complete(token=T1) { residency.set(token) } Evict path clears residency and bumps epoch. Callback currently has no epoch check.

Sara: so callback can race and re-set residency after eviction. we need a demarcation between prefetch lifecycle and eviction semantics.

Lee: options: A) make callback epoch-aware and do CAS with epoch+token; B) eviction subscribes and cancels in-flight callbacks; C) prefetch returns a cancellable handle and eviction cancels it.

Anjali: tradeoffs — A is smallest surface change (residency becomes {epoch, token}), B requires a pub/sub shim and edgecase handling across RPCs, C couples lifecycle and increases cancellation surface.

Mike H: also concerned about metrics/observability. need counters for callback_ignored_due_to_epoch and prefetch_cancelled so we can debug flakes.

Sara: for correctness I'm leaning A + TTL on residency. callback should check epoch and bail if stale. example pseudo:

```
if (callback_epoch != current_epoch) {
  metrics.inc("callback_stale");
  return;
}
residency.compare_exchange(expected=null_or_old, desired=(epoch, token))
```

This avoids reintroducing tokens after eviction.

Lee: note CAS still needs careful semantics: eviction might set null between check and CAS. tests should fuzz interleavings where eviction and callback contend.

Mike H: good point — add unit tests with race harness and an integration smoke that ramps eviction frequency. I'll sketch the RFC: change residency shape, epoch-guard callbacks, optionally plumb cancellable handles for future. include telemetry and tests.

Anjali: can you add a brief plan for rollout? toggled feature flag + canary + metric checks (callback_stale rate). I can help write the fuzz tests.

Mike H: will draft RFC today and ping for review. thanks! :thumbsup: 

deploy-bot: New RFC posted: https://go.redwood/rfc/prefetch-residency-epoch (perf/eviction section added)

Anjali: saw it, adding test harness to the PR.

Sara: also let's document the compat contract for third-party callers: prefetch callbacks must be idempotent. small blurb in docs will help.

Mike H: yep will add. thanks everyone.
